Takes the sign-in state (single use), exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier and reads a verified email: Google from the `id_token` (signature, audience, nonce and `email_verified` checked), GitHub from the primary verified address of `/user/emails`. The user is matched by (provider, subject), then by verified email (the identity is linked), else created. Needs `manage` (owners and admins; 403 `forbidden` otherwise, 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). A public email domain answers `domain_not_allowed`; a slug other than the current one answers `slug_immutable`. Audited as `org.updated`.

get.description: Lists the organization's pending invitations, newest first, including expired ones that can still be resent. Owners and admins only (403 `forbidden`).
get.summary: List pending invitations

post.description: Invites up to 50 addresses, each with the admin, member or viewer role, and emails each a link to `/invite/{token}` that works for 7 days. Owners and admins only (403 `forbidden`). Addresses of members are skipped (`already_member`); an address with a pending invitation gets a new one in its place (`replaced`). Returns one result per address, in request order. Each email sent is audited as `invitation.sent`.

delete.description: Revokes the pending invitation; its link stops working. Owners and admins only (403 `forbidden`). An invitation that was accepted or already revoked answers `invite_expired`.

post.description: Emails the pending invitation again with a new link that works for 7 days; the previous link stops working. Owners and admins only (403 `forbidden`). An invitation can be emailed at most once every 5 minutes (`rate_limited` with `retry_after`). An invitation that was accepted or revoked answers `invite_expired`. Audited as `invitation.sent`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; mirrors `retry_after`.

post.description: Makes the signed-in user a `member` of the organization when it has domain join on and lists the domain of the user's verified email among its allowed domains, and returns the organization with the user's role. Answers `forbidden` (403) otherwise, and for an organization that does not exist. Idempotent: a user who already belongs to it gets it back with their current role and nothing changes. Audited as `member.joined`.
post.summary: Join an organization by verified email domain

post.description: Removes the signed-in user from the organization. Needs `view` (any member; 404 `not_found` otherwise). The last owner cannot leave (`last_owner`): transfer ownership or delete the organization first. Audited as `member.removed`.

get.description: Lists the members of the organization with their user, role, when they joined and when they last signed in, oldest member first. Needs `view` (any member); 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view.
get.summary: List organization members

delete.description: Removes the member from the organization. Needs `manage_members` (owners and admins); only owners can remove an owner (403 `forbidden`). Removing the last owner answers `last_owner`; a user who is not a member answers `member_gone`. Audited as `member.removed`.

patch.description: Sets the member's role. Needs `manage_members` (owners and admins); only owners can make someone an owner or change an owner's role (403 `forbidden`). Demoting the last owner answers `last_owner`; a user who is not a member answers `member_gone`. Audited as `member.role_changed`.

get.description: Lists the organization's active projects with their environments, ordered by name. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project or organization does not exist or the user is not a member of the organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.
get.summary: List an organization's projects

post.description: Creates a project with its environments in the organization. Owners, admins and members only. Project slugs are globally unique: a reserved or used slug answers `slug_taken` (409) with up to three free `suggestions`. Emits `project.created`. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project or organization does not exist or the user is not a member of the organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

delete.description: Removes the organization's OIDC connection; its members sign in by email, social or passkey again. Owners only (403 `forbidden` otherwise, 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). Answers `sso_not_configured` (409) when there is no connection. Audited as `sso.deleted`.

get.description: Returns the organization's OIDC connection with the redirect URI to register with the identity provider. The client secret is write-only and shows as `********`. Owners only (403 `forbidden` otherwise, 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). Answers `sso_not_configured` (409) when there is no connection.
get.summary: Get the organization's SSO connection

put.description: Saves the organization's OIDC connection. The client secret is stored encrypted; omit it (or send `********`) to keep the stored one, a new connection needs one (`invalid_request`). Owners only (403 `forbidden` otherwise, 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). Turning `enforce` on needs the caller to have signed in through this connection since it was created (`sso_untested`), and a domain another organization enforces SSO for answers `sso_domain_taken`. A public email domain answers `domain_not_allowed`. Audited as `sso.updated`.
put.summary: Create or replace the organization's SSO connection

post.description: Runs OIDC discovery on `issuer` (default: the saved connection's) and reports the identity provider's metadata. A provider that cannot be reached or serves an unusable document answers 200 with `ok: false` and an `error`. Owners only (403 `forbidden` otherwise, 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). Answers `sso_not_configured` (409) without an `issuer` when there is no connection.

Makes the member an owner and the signed-in owner an admin, in one step. Owners only (403 `forbidden`; 404 `not_found` for an organization the user cannot view). A user who is not a member answers `member_gone`; transferring to oneself answers `invalid_request`. Audited as `member.role_changed` for each member whose role changes.

patch.description: Renames the project. Owners, admins and members only. A slug other than the current one answers `slug_immutable`. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project or organization does not exist or the user is not a member of the organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

get.description: Lists the project's API keys, revoked ones included, newest first. Keys are shown by prefix; the full key is never returned again. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project does not exist or the user is not a member of its organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

post.description: Issues an API key for the project and returns it in full, once: only its hash is stored. Owners, admins and members only. A project has at most `ingest.max_keys_per_project` (default 50) active keys: past that it answers `key_limit_reached` (409) until one is revoked or expires. Audited as `api_key.created`. Needs a sign-in less than `identity.sensitive_action_max_age` (10 minutes) old: an older session answers `reauth_required` (403) and the user signs in again. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project does not exist or the user is not a member of its organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

delete.description: Revokes the key: the ingest edge and query API reject it from then on (every process drops it from its cache through Valkey). Revoking a revoked key changes nothing; an id the project does not have answers `api_key_gone` (410). Owners, admins and members only. Audited as `api_key.revoked`. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project does not exist or the user is not a member of its organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

put.description: Replaces whether the key may create apps (the apps:create scope) and which apps it may send data for (null: every app), and sets its ingest rate limit when `rate_limit_per_minute` is sent (0 removes it). Every process forgets the cached key, so the change applies to the next request. A revoked key or an id the project does not have answers `api_key_gone` (410); an app id the project does not have answers `invalid_request`. Owners, admins and members only. Audited as `api_key.updated`. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project does not exist or the user is not a member of its organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

The rest of each batch was stored. Needs `view` on the project (any member, including viewers). A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

post.description: Acknowledges an app the SDK created, so it no longer shows as "New app detected". Audited as `app.acknowledged`. Needs `manage_capture` on the project (project admins, organization owners and admins; 403 `forbidden` for other members). A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

Hides the app. Data naming it later un-archives it (audited as `app.restored` with `by` sdk). The default app cannot be archived (`invalid_request`). Audited as `app.archived`. Needs `manage_capture` on the project (project admins, organization owners and admins; 403 `forbidden` for other members). A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

Merges the app into `into` (for typos and forks): the app is archived, its slug becomes an alias of `into` and data naming it lands in `into` from now on. Data already stored is not rewritten and stays under the old app. `into` must be active and differ from the app; the default app cannot be merged. Audited as `app.merged`. Needs `manage_capture` on the project (project admins, organization owners and admins; 403 `forbidden` for other members). A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

Brings back an archived, merged or deleted app. A merged app's slug stops routing to the app it was merged into. Restoring a deleted app whose slug a newer app took answers `slug_taken` (409). Audited as `app.restored`. Needs `manage_capture` on the project (project admins, organization owners and admins; 403 `forbidden` for other members). A project the caller cannot view, or an app it does not have, answers 404 `not_found`.

get.description: Returns the server-side privacy policy of the project, or of one of its apps with `?app=`, and the built-in defaults. The ingest edge masks, before storing a record, the values of matching query parameters in `raw_path`, captured headers, JSON body fields (string and number values) and `key=value` pairs in log messages, using the built-in defaults plus the project's policy plus the record's app's policy. Patterns only add to the defaults. Edges pick a change up within the app cache TTL (`ingest.app_cache_ttl`, 60 s by default). An unknown app answers `invalid_request`. Answers `forbidden` (403) when the project does not exist or the user is not a member of its organization, so the cases cannot be told apart.

delete.description: Deletes the account with a 30-day grace period: it is hidden at once, every session is revoked, and it is removed for good after `delete_after`. Refused with `owner_transfer_required` while the user is the only owner of an organization. Audited as `user.deleted`.

get.description: Returns the signed-in user's profile, preferences, onboarding state and how the current session was authenticated (`amr`).
get.summary: Get the signed-in user

patch.description: Updates the name and avatar, and merges `preferences` into the stored ones (keys not sent stay unchanged). Audited as `user.updated`.

get.description: Returns in one call what the app shell needs: the user, their organizations with their role and each organization's projects and environments, the last opened project, the onboarding state and, per project, the actions the user may perform. Capabilities are computed with one SpiceDB `CheckBulkPermissions` call; when SpiceDB cannot answer, the call fails with `authz_unavailable` rather than returning partial capabilities. A user deleted while their access token is still valid answers `session_expired`.
get.summary: Get the signed-in user's context

post.description: Emails a 6-digit code to `new_email`; confirm it with `/users/me/email/confirm`. A new request replaces the pending one. Answers `email_taken` when another account uses the address, and `invalid_request` when it is already the user's.
post.summary: Start changing the signed-in user's email

post.description: Checks the code sent to the new address and makes it the account's verified email. Every other session is signed out and the old address gets a security alert. Audited as `email.changed`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; mirrors `retry_after`.

post.summary: Confirm the signed-in user's new email

get.description: Lists the Google and GitHub accounts connected to the signed-in user, oldest first. Connect one with `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth/{provider}/start?intent=link`.
get.summary: List my connected accounts

delete.description: Disconnects one of the signed-in user's Google or GitHub accounts; it can no longer be used to sign in. Email always remains a sign-in method, so the last connected account can be disconnected too. Answers 410 `oauth_identity_gone` for an id that is not one of the user's connected accounts. Audited as `oauth.unlinked`; the user is emailed a security alert.

get.description: Lists the active organizations the signed-in user is not a member of that have domain join on and list the domain of the user's verified email among their allowed domains, ordered by name. An unverified email or one at a public email provider (gmail.com, outlook.com…) matches none.
get.summary: List organizations I can join

patch.description: Saves where the user is in onboarding so a refresh resumes there: `step` replaces the stored step, `answers` is merged key by key into the stored answers (org_slug, project_slug, language, runtime, method, invited, api_key_id), and `completed` finishes or reopens onboarding. Returns the resulting state; `GET /api/v1/users/me/context` reports the same step and completion. Unknown fields fail validation (`422`).
patch.summary: Save the signed-in user's onboarding progress

get.description: Lists the signed-in user's passkeys, oldest first, with name, authenticator vendor, backup state and when each was added and last used.
get.summary: List my passkeys

delete.description: Removes one of the signed-in user's passkeys; it can no longer be used to sign in. Answers 410 `passkey_gone` for an id that is not one of the user's passkeys. Audited as `passkey.removed`; the user is emailed a security alert.

patch.description: Renames one of the signed-in user's passkeys. Answers 400 `invalid_request` for a blank name and 410 `passkey_gone` for an id that is not one of the user's passkeys. Audited as `passkey.renamed`.

post.description: Public; authenticated by a fresh email code sent to the account's address. Undoes `DELETE /api/v1/users/me` while the account is inside its grace period (sign-in answers `account_deleting` with `delete_after` until then). No session is issued: sign in again afterwards. Audited as `user.restored`. A wrong code, an address with nothing to restore, and an account past its grace period all answer `invalid_code`. Rate-limited per email address.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; mirrors `retry_after`.

get.description: Lists the signed-in user's live sessions (one per sign-in), most recently active first, with device label, IP and activity times. The session the request was made with has `current: true`.
get.summary: List my sessions

post.description: Ends every session of the signed-in user except the one the request was made with: their refresh tokens stop working at once and their access tokens within seconds. Audited as `session.revoked`.

delete.description: Ends one of the signed-in user's sessions (it may be the current one): its refresh token stops working at once and its access tokens within seconds. Audited as `session.revoked`. Answers 204 also for an unknown or already ended session.

post.description: Sent by every SDK process on start and then about once a minute. Records the instance as last seen now (the app shows as reporting for 5 minutes) and answers the app's remote capture policy, which the SDK applies until the next heartbeat. At most one heartbeat per instance every 10 seconds; a faster one answers 429 with Retry-After. On 503 the SDK keeps its previous policy. A body with an `api_key` field at any depth is rejected with 422.

200.description: Recorded; the body carries the capture policy

403.description: API key lacks the ingest scope, may not create the app it names, or is limited to other apps

409.description: The app was deleted less than 30 days ago; restore it from Apps

422.description: Invalid payload or an app limit reached

429.description: Heartbeat of this instance less than 10 seconds after the previous one; retry after Retry-After

post.summary: Report an SDK instance is alive and fetch the capture policy

post.description: Sent by the SDKs once per process start: framework and versions, the route templates the framework declares (at most 2000 are kept) and the effective SDK config. Replaces the previous report of the app in the environment, and records the framework on the app when it has none. A body with an `api_key` field at any depth is rejected with 422.

403.description: API key lacks the ingest scope, may not create the app it names, or is limited to other apps

409.description: The app was deleted less than 30 days ago; restore it from Apps

422.description: Invalid payload, an app limit reached, or an api_key field
